ctx.x: Who would be in some of the bands?

Well, as I, as I was gonna know them, that was Chris Keller's band, it was Walter Blue's band, it was Buddy Petit's band, Joe Petit's Columbia, Columbia band, it was Longhead Bob's band, the Maple Leaf, Leaf band, Emanuel Perez's band, Hippolyte Charles' band, that was that, that was the Silver Maple Leaf band.
Who was involved with the Blues band? Do you remember any of those guys?

items.q: tradition of New Orleans trumpet playing from Buddy Petit, Freddie Keppard, Bunk Johnson... and he heard them

ctx.x: what was the difference in their style?

Well, there's a big difference. one was lyrical which from, from a classical vein, technically musical because Bix was a, uh, was interested in concert music and Debussy and Ravel and his thing was semi-classical, that In the Mist and a couple of piano pieces he wrote which had a, a great significance of creative inventiveness but based from a European, a classical vein where Louis stuff was so black out of the Baptist Church and out of the honky tonks and, uh, out of, uh, a tradition of New Orleans trumpet…

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Buddy Petit had more followers than anybody... It was Buddy Petit. I’ll tell you that.

ctx.x: That’s right. See King Oliver. In those days we’d have maybe six or seven guys following right within hearing distance, not to disrupt the second line, to listen to King Oliver blow, wait until he play his chorus, and he’d blow it at them. “Hey Joe, put that riff in there.” Him and Kid Rena, he had his followers, and Buddy Petit had more followers than anybody.

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: My little uncle, Willie, would whisper... 'That's Mister Buddy Petit.' ... there on the corner would be maybe the Superior Band, or Buddy Petit's band... playing out there. And you'd go out there to look at the music.

ctx.x: He had a society type band, didn't he.

Yes. And that was... You looked up on him; you saw him in the street. And these people were all celebrated when you'd see as a kid. My little uncle, Willie, would whisper [SOTTO VOCE] "That's Mister Manuel Perez. That's Mister Buddy Petit. That's Kid Rena. That's Chris Kelly. That's ...(?)...." (?) had this great band, you'd hear him. And I'm listening to all that.
